title: The Wager to Anger Hillel
text:
The Talmud tells of two men who made a bet of four hundred zuz, a large sum. One of them claimed he could make Hillel lose his temper, and the other said it could not be done.

The challenger chose his moment carefully: a Friday afternoon, when Hillel was washing his hair to prepare for the Sabbath. He walked past the door shouting, "Who here is Hillel? Who here is Hillel?" Hillel wrapped himself in a cloak and came out. "My son, what do you need?" "I have a question. Why are the heads of the Babylonians round?" Hillel answered patiently that it was because they lacked skilled midwives.

The man went away, waited, and came back shouting again, this time asking why the people of Palmyra had bleary eyes. Hillel came out again and answered: because they live among the sands. A third time he came, asking why the Africans had wide feet. Because they live in marshy land, Hillel said.

At last the man said, "I have many more questions, but I am afraid you will get angry." Hillel sat down. "Ask them all." Instead the man burst out, "May there not be many like you in Israel! I have lost four hundred zuz because of you." Hillel replied that he should watch his temper: Hillel was worth his losing four hundred zuz and four hundred more, and Hillel would still not get angry.
lesson: Answer tiresome or provocative people from your own calm, not from their tone. Patience costs little and usually wins more than irritation does.
people: Hillel, a man who bet he could anger him
